minutes.headline: Sewer Commission set conditions for the unpermitted 384 Mass Ave connection and clashed over a member's counsel visit.
minutes.summary: The commission discussed the unpermitted sewer connection at 384 Mass Ave and agreed to require a surveyed as-built plan, excavation of key points, and a meeting with the contractor. It also began the FY22 budget in a simplified town format, planned an assistant for the sewer office, and voted on an irrigation meter extension, a school bill, and a crossroads assessment commitment. A heated exchange occurred when the chair accused a member of violating the counsel-hours policy.

public_comment.topic: A resident (Mr. Paschalls, per the captions) said the Finance Committee will begin budget work soon and welcomed the sewer budget format changes.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission agreed to expect a surveyed as-built plan, excavation of key points and a contractor meeting for the unpermitted 384 Mass Ave connection.
Members reviewed a simplified town-style FY22 sewer budget format; the office administrator will use the old format this year, with a draft due January 26.
The chair proposed an assistant for the sewer office in the FY22 budget, possibly part-time at first, subject to Personnel Committee and Town Meeting process.
Three votes were taken on an irrigation meter extension, a school irrigation meter bill and a Crossroad privilege fee commitment; the results are not audible in the recording.
A dispute over the counsel-hours policy ended without resolution, and a revisit of the policy was suggested.

why_it_matters: Sewer connection rules, privilege fees and meter billing set what property owners are charged and when, and an unpermitted connection can affect others on the system.
The FY22 sewer budget format and a possible new staff position will shape the costs that reach sewer users and, through Town Meeting, the town budget.
watch_next: January 26 meeting: draft FY22 sewer budget expected.
February 11: annual report due; maintenance plan comments deferred to the February meeting.
